title: Soft Burst Lifecycle and Throughput Certainty Layer
author: Ava Martinez
body: Context: customers running Dedicated capacity reported intermittent SLO violations during multi-tenant microbursts. Current burst token pools provide capacity but lack lifecycle semantics and cross-pool telemetry, leading to either wasted reserved headroom or aggressive throttling. This PR introduces the Soft Burst Lifecycle (SBL) controller and a complementary Throughput Certainty Layer (TCL) that together provide more predictable throughput guarantees while preserving opportunistic burstability. Design summary: 1) Soft Burst Lifecycle: tokens now have three states (staged, active, decayed). Staged tokens are prebooked warmlets with time-to-activate metadata; active tokens contribute to admission decisions; decayed tokens are shadowed and reclaimed gradually. This reduces instantaneous pressure on the scheduler and avoids large eviction storms. 2) Throughput Certainty Layer: a per-tenant moving-window throughput contract evaluator that tracks committed throughput, observed fulfillment, and a confidence metric. The evaluator produces a certainty score used by the headroom allocator to prefer fulfilling contractual throughput before opportunistic bursts. 3) Telemetry normalizer: new histograms and summary metrics (sbl.token_latency_ms, tcl.confidence, tcl.fulfillment_pct, sbl.decay_rate) plus lineage tags for pool/zone/tenant to allow downstream rollups and SLI dashboards. 4) Backwards compatibility: existing token APIs preserved. New token lifecycle messages emitted on existing event stream with a version flag. 5) Control knobs: configurable staged-to-active grace, decay half-life, and certainty weight. Implementation notes: changes touch autoscaler, admission controller, reservation ledger, and telemetry exporter. We added a lightweight in-memory windowed evaluator in the admission path with bounded CPU impact and strict observer sampling for heavy tenants. Tests and rollout: unit tests for state transitions and evaluator logic. Integration test harness simulates mixed committed/opportunistic workloads and asserts SLO adherence across 95th percentile latency and fulfillment gap at 99th percentile. Staged rollout: enabled behind feature flag rollout.sbl_tcl by pool; can be toggled per-tenant. Migration plan: default knobs tuned to conservative values for first two weeks, then automatically relaxed by the controller if utilization is low. Checklist: - [x] design doc attached (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1876-soft-burst-lifecycle-design) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry + dashboard panels - [x] rollout feature flag and per-pool enablement - [x] docs snippet for ops teams - [x] canary run in reserved-us-west cluster Outcome: after canary we observed a 22% reduction in tail SLO violations under synthetic spike tests and a 9% improvement in committed throughput fulfillment. Caveats: extremely bursty traffic where tenants have zero commitments can still see higher variance; tuned decay-rate knob addresses most cases. Follow-ups: expose decay and certainty weight via Console, add historical replay for analytic reconstruction.

release_notes: Introduce Soft Burst Lifecycle (staged/active/decayed tokens) and Throughput Certainty Layer to improve throughput fulfillment and reduce tail SLO violations. Adds new telemetry metrics and per-pool feature flag. Rollout behind feature flag; conservative defaults applied.
